Prevention: Do not plant in areas over 900 ft above sea level.
Apply best cultural practices such as good drainage, proper weed control, pruning, shade and wind break management
Remove from the field and destroy, infected pods and branches
Monitoring: The disease affects the pod and the beans of cocoa
December fields are fruiting and should be monitored at least twice weekly
In the initial stages of the disease a brownish/dark soft spot is observe on the fruit.
Within 7 days the entire pod will turn black
Action should be taken as soon as the first spot in observed
Observe stem for cankers which indicates the presence of the disease
Restrictions: Wear protective clothing when applying fungicides eg. repirators, rubber boots, gloves etc. ing.
Sprayers are known to consume fruits whiles spraying.
